stem:
Ethoxyethane, $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OC}_2\text{H}_5$, can dissolve both in water and in octan-1-ol. The expression and numerical value for the partition coefficient of ethoxyethane between water and octan-1-ol are given. Water and octan-1-ol are immiscible.

$$K_{\text{pc}} = \frac{\text{concentration of } \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OC}_2\text{H}_5 \text{ in octan-1-ol}}{\text{concentration of } \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OC}_2\text{H}_5 \text{ in water}} = 6.760 \text{ at } 20^{\circ}\text{C}$$

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
In an experiment, octan-1-ol at $20^{\circ}\text{C}$ is added to a solution of ethoxyethane in water at $20^{\circ}\text{C}$. The mixture is analysed immediately and a value of $K_{\text{pc}}$ is calculated.

The calculation is performed correctly; the value calculated is 5.625.

Explain why the value calculated is less than 6.760.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem: A second experiment is performed and the value of $K_{\text{pc}}$ is found to be 6.760. The concentration of ethoxyethane in the octan-1-ol layer is $7.62\text{ g dm}^{-3}$.
parts.text: Calculate the concentration, in $\text{g dm}^{-3}$, of ethoxyethane in the aqueous layer.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
$100\text{ cm}^3$ of the octan-1-ol layer is taken and shaken with $100\text{ cm}^3$ of water.

Calculate the maximum amount, in mol, of ethoxyethane that can be extracted into the water.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem:
An aqueous solution of lead(II) nitrate is mixed with an aqueous solution of sodium iodide. A yellow precipitate of lead(II) iodide is formed and is filtered out, leaving solution $\mathbf{X}$.

The concentration of $\text{Pb}^{2+}$ in solution $\mathbf{X}$ is $5.68 \times 10^{-3}\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$.

The concentration of $\text{I}^{-}$ in solution $\mathbf{X}$ is $4.20 \times 10^{-4}\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$.
parts.text:
Use these data to calculate a value for the solubility product, $K_{\text{sp}}$, of lead(II) iodide.

State the units of $K_{\text{sp}}$.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
Potassium iodide is very soluble in water.

Describe and explain what is seen if a few drops of saturated potassium iodide solution are added to a portion of solution $\mathbf{X}$.
